$comment:
PLACEHOLDER RECORDS — the quotations the subscriptions were sold on. Stands in for GET /api/v1/admin/quotations/ (which is ALREADY LIVE, via AdminOpsService.quotations). SHADOWING A LIVE ENDPOINT IS NORMALLY THE ONE THING THIS CONVENTION FORBIDS — membership-plans.json was deleted for exactly that. It is here for the same reason `invoices.json` beside it is, and its $comment says the same thing: Finance is being built frontend-first, and its cross-module READS are seeded together so the deal → quotation → invoice → subscription chain resolves with no backend running. Seeding only half of it would leave the chain broken in the middle, which is worse than seeding all of it. Both files come out in the SAME commit, when Finance moves onto AdminOpsService.

WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR: the quotation is where a sale's SHAPE is agreed — the plan, the term, the total, and how many installments it is paid in. The invoice is one installment of it. Recording a subscription should therefore ask for a business and read the rest, instead of making an operator retype four numbers that already exist on two documents. `installments: 1` is a complete payment; there is no separate flag for it.

SHAPE: a projection of the live QuotationRow (src/api/modules/adminOps), flattened to the one plan line every quotation on this chain carries. The live row nests it in `items[]` with kind:'plan'; the fields are named identically so the swap is a mapping and not a redesign.

quotations.$comment: THE INSTALLMENTS ARE NOT EQUAL and the invoices raised against this prove it: ₹59,000 (cancelled), ₹2,47,800 and ₹6,37,200. A quotation agrees a TOTAL and a COUNT; the chain decides what each invoice is for. Any code that assumes total ÷ count will disagree with this row, which is the point of it being in the seed.

Two installments agreed, ONE invoice raised. The second is raised when it falls due, which is why a quotation's installment count and the number of invoices that exist for it are different questions — and why the record dialog must read the count from here rather than from counting documents.

ACCEPTED, INVOICED, AND NOT YET RECORDED — the happy path. Pick Iyer Woodworks in Record a subscription and everything below the business comes from here and from invoice 00092: Growth, 12 months, complete payment, ₹2,95,000. Nothing is typed.

THE MULTI-INSTALLMENT WALKABLE PATH. Three installments of ₹21,240; the first is invoice 00094 and the other two are not raised yet. Recording from this quotation must produce a three-row schedule without anybody choosing the number.

ALREADY RECORDED as SUB-0110 — the demo of what a complete-payment chain looks like once it has been through the dialog. Quotation agreed one payment of ₹28,320, invoice 00098 billed it, the money arrived, the receipt was issued. Nothing here is walkable; it is here so the finished shape can be read without recording one first.

ALREADY RECORDED as SUB-0111 — the demo of a running installment plan. Three of ₹70,800: the first is paid and receipted, the second is invoiced and waiting, the third has no invoice because the chain has not raised it yet. That is the ordinary mid-life state of an installment subscription and it is the one most screens have to get right.

quotations.rejectReason: Went with a competitor on price.
quotations.$comment: REJECTED, and its invoice was cancelled. It is in the seed so the dialog has to decide what to do with a quotation that was never accepted — the answer is that it is not offered, because a subscription cannot be recorded on a sale that did not happen.
